element.name: Mosaic
element.documentation: MOSAIC root element.

element.name: ContainerMetaData
element.documentation: Document description

element.name: ObjectsCounter
element.documentation: Total number of objects in the document.

element.name: ObjectsTotalSize
element.documentation: Total size of (uncompressed) objects in the document.

element.name: CompressionMethod
element.documentation: Name of the algorithm that should be used to decompress objects, or "none" if they are stored in plain.

enum.label: zstd (at least one frame) using a pre-trained dictionary provided in CompressionData

element.name: CompressionData
element.documentation: Decompression-specific data (for example, a dictionary).

element.name: Comment
element.documentation: An arbitrary-length presentation of the file. This is intended for curated archive extracts. Note that a file can contain more than one comment element: this can be useful to separate different documents presenting the file. For example we advise to attach this XML to MOSAIC files intended for publication.

element.name: EndOfTilesOffset
element.documentation: Offset (number of bytes from the beginning of the file) of the first top element after `ContainerMetaData` that is not a `Tile`. This allows random-access-oriented readers to skip directly to indexes.

element.name: Tile
element.documentation: Objects should be dispatched in smaller tile and each tile should contain a CRC32 element. In case of data corruption, this granularity will be easier to recover. We suggest to avoid tiles bigger than 32MB. A tile should either contain multiple Object element, or only one Objects element that compresses objects together according to what's described in CompressionMethod.

element.name: Object
element.documentation: A single object, compressed according to CompressionMethod.

element.name: Index
element.documentation: Index for fast lookup of objects.

element.name: IdxDescription
element.documentation: Description of this index' key semantics and its map format, including a pURL and a SWHID of the decoder algorithm and maybe hints on the class to use and its parameters, if needed.

enum.label: Key is object's SHA1 (20-bytes array), Map is an FMPHGO MPH
Key is the SHA1 of the object prefixed as in git (20-bytes array), Map is an FMPHGO MPH
Key is object's SHA256(32-bytes array), Map is an FMPHGO MPH
Key is object's blake2s256 checksum (32-bytes array), Map is an FMPHGO MPH

element.name: IdxUnrolled
element.documentation: Unrolled index entries: all `(Key, Offset)` pairs present in the document. Order should match how `Map` places keys.

element.name: Key
element.documentation: Key for an index entry. All keys in a given `Index` should have the same size.

element.name: Offset
element.documentation:
Offset in file for an index entry. All offset in a given `Index` entries should have the same size.
When using `Object` (individual compression), an object's offset is the distance in bytes between the start of the file and the start of the `Object` tag. When using `Objects` (multi-objects compression), an offset should combine the distance in bytes between the start of the file and the start of the `Objects` tag with the rank (or similar) of the object in decompressed data. `IdxDescription` can provide precisions.

element.name: GoToConflicts
element.documentation:
This element should replace an `Offset` when an key is associated to more than one object, to notify readers they should find all possible offsets in a `Conflict` element.
This element does not carry any data, so its length must be zero. Because key-offset pairs below `IdxUnrolled` must have the same length, writers should append a void element of the correct length after `GoToConflicts`.

element.name: IdxUnrolledEntrySize
element.documentation: If the mapping technique assumes that index entries have a fixed size, this size should be defined here (in bytes, including EBML wrappers).

element.name: MapContainer
element.documentation: This wrapper element allow us to put a CRC32 before the serialized `Map`. Readers should check that `Map`'s content matches its checksum before deserializing it.

element.name: Map
element.documentation: An efficient mapping technique of keys to their position in the index or in payload. We prepare for two techniques. First, minimal perfect hashes that map a key to their rank in IdxUnrolled (which can be transposed to an offset thanks to IdxUnrolledEntrySize). Second, static functions that map directly a key to its offset in Payload.

element.name: Conflicts
element.documentation: This element enumerates key conflicts, if any.

element.name: Conflict
element.documentation: A single key conflict.

element.name: ConflictingKey
element.documentation: The conflicting key.

element.name: ConflictingOffset
element.documentation: One of the possible offsets for the conflicting key.
